market_holds: Spot $4.695 at the 18:08 UTC seal (baseline). The front-expiry straddle implies an 18.6% move over 24 days, which is about 15.5% for the event once ordinary volatility is taken out. The stock is down 17% over 20 sessions, 76.5% off its 52-week high and 50% since the Q2 print ($9.35 close on 2026-08-26, now $4.66 on Yahoo bars). That fall is mostly a sector move: since 2026-08-27, FINV is down 38%, LX 55% and KWEB 19%, so it is not tied to Qfin-specific news. Market cap is about $571M (121.6M ADS on Yahoo), below the company's stated RMB10.6B of cash and short-term investments. Yahoo's enterprise value is negative. The stock trades at about 1.8x the FY2027 consensus of RMB18.14/ADS. Q3 consensus is RMB3.41/ADS (about RMB415M, one analyst, cut from 7.12 in the last 7 days) against company guidance of RMB400-500M non-GAAP (RMB360-460M GAAP). Q4 consensus is RMB3.31/ADS (about RMB400M, cut from 5.68 last week). EarningsWhispers' USD consensus is $0.46 EPS on $439.7M revenue. Short interest is 2.0% of float and falling (1.97M from 2.77M), and put/call open interest is 0.06, so the book is long and call-heavy rather than crowded short. Buybacks have been suspended since late June. On the opening print, the last four prints moved -13% (2025-11), -4% (2026-03), +10% (2026-05, +25% by the close) and -15% (2026-08). The stock trades on the next-quarter profit guide and the credit trend (FPD, C-M2, 30-day collection).
view: This print is the sector's first read on September and October credit, about a week before FINV, XYF and LX report. In August, the then-CEO said credit had reversed suddenly: FPD3/FPD7 up about 20% month on month, C-M2 up about 25%. He said Q3 volume would fall meaningfully, external funding costs would keep rising and normalisation would take at least two to three quarters. The Q3 guide of RMB400-500M was called preliminary and subject to material change. Several things have arrived since that call and so are not in that guide. There was a nationwide clean-up of debt collection in Q3. The online financial-marketing rules took effect on 2026-09-30. Banks cut partner lists further (one bank went from 56 partners to 10), and local window guidance reportedly caps guarantee-type business at 25%. The former CRO became CEO on 2026-09-21, and this is his first quarter: a conservative Q4 guide and front-loaded provisions are the natural move. So I expect the Q4 guide to land at or below the freshly cut ~RMB400M consensus, with C-M2 still elevated. Against that, the price already discounts far worse than any plausible guide. At about 1.8x the FY27 consensus and below net cash, a Q4 of RMB250-350M is not a disaster against this price. The Q1 2026 print showed what 'risk better than feared' does from a washed-out level: +10% at the open, +25% by the close. Short interest is low, so there is no squeeze fuel, but the call-heavy book is fragile either way. I cannot see the deciding inputs (September and October FPD and collections, the Q4 number, whether a 2027 buyback is announced). No fresh dated Qfin or industry credit series turned up after the August call. My lean is mildly negative on the guide but offset by how much the price already holds, so there is no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the Q4 profit guide and the September/October credit trend, and neither is visible beforehand. Qualitatively, the inputs since the August call (the collection clean-up, the 30 September marketing rules, bank partner cuts, a former-CRO CEO in his first quarter) point to a guide at or below the freshly cut ~RMB400M Q4 consensus. But the price, at about 1.8x FY27 consensus and below net cash, after a 50% sector-wide fall, plausibly already holds a worse outcome than that. I cannot show which side of that line the release lands on with 65% confidence.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 non-GAAP guide at or above ~RMB400M with management saying C-M2/FPD peaked in August-September and improved in October, or a new 2027 buyback authorisation, would make this a likely sharp up-move. A Q4 guide well under RMB300M or a loss, or a statement that collections keep worsening, would make it a down-move.

self_critique: The case for down is stronger than 45 suggests on one reading. Three of the last four prints opened lower. The new CEO is a risk officer in his first quarter, with every incentive to kitchen-sink. Everything dated since the August call (the collection clean-up, the marketing rules, bank partner cuts, LX flagging a loss) is negative. The market cut this stock 19% last time from a level that also looked cheap. The case for up is that the price, below net cash at under 2x forward consensus with the sector down 40-55%, already holds a guide much worse than consensus. Q1 2026 showed a +25% day from a similar setup, and this is the sector's first data point, so relief can be large. The two cases roughly offset, and I cannot show the line landing on either side with 65% confidence.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was the most useful step: it showed the 50% fall is a sector and tape move, which kept me from reading it either as proof of priced-in or as momentum. P4 and P7 pushed toward estimating the hidden line from inputs, but with no post-call platform data and no peer reports yet, the inputs only gave a qualitative lean that the price's depth plausibly already holds.
